title: SymDrive: Realistic and Controllable Driving Simulator via Symmetric Auto-regressive Online Restoration

control_signal.value: Vehicle motion parameters (rotation and translation over time) of Gaussian-splat vehicles, plus inserted 3D vehicle assets; trajectories come from external rule-based or learning-based traffic controllers.

control_mechanism.value: Direct control of per-vehicle pose in a 3DGS scene; inserted vehicles are harmonized by a training-free diffusion inpainting step (masked region, dual-view context) and appearance fine-tuning of color and opacity.

base_model.value: StreetGS 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction plus Flux.1-dev flow-matching diffusion fine-tuned with LoRA rank 128 for symmetric dual-view, auto-regressive novel-view restoration.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Dataset (eight scenes, 40 consecutive frames each) for evaluation; nuScenes qualitative only; 3DRealCar vehicle models for insertion.

metrics.value: NTA-IoU, NTL-IoU and FID for novel-view rendering; FID before and after vehicle insertion; rendering FPS versus vehicle count.

controllability_evidence.value: Qualitative only: dense traffic via SUMO and aggressive lane changes via a learning-based trajectory simulator are rendered (Fig. 6); inserted vehicles show better lighting match. Novel-view FID 74.82 at 3 m lateral shift is a rendering result.

stated_limitations.value: Distant objects with sparse pixels cause temporal inconsistencies; the system lacks rigid physics-based collision constraints; future work on video diffusion and a physics engine.

notes: Primarily a rendering and asset-editing paper; behavior control is delegated to external traffic simulators, so it is not a controllable behavior generator. No quantitative controllability metric in packet.
